pf.license.need: where the state's rules require it: a food service permit for the restaurant, and a caterer's permit for cooking at a customer's place or an event; a liquor license for any bar service
pf.license.holder: the business holds the permits; each person holds a food handler card or an alcohol server permit only where the state's rules require it
pf.license.ask: the permit number and the name on it, from the restaurant's state form
pf.license.check: a person on Rosie's team checks the state's or the county's lookup within 1 business day; where no lookup exists, identity plus what the business says
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.renewals: Rosie reminds 30 days before a permit's date and checks again on it
pf.license.insurance: liability insurance for events at a customer's place or a venue, when the venue or the state's rules ask for proof

pf.services.shape: tables by party size and sitting (the table is the bookable space, not a person: the owner lists each space and its size at sign-up); the menu and its prices show; cooking at a customer's home or event is its own service

pf.services.capacity: seats and tables, typed once: which tables join for big parties; the long table seats 6 to 10, the back room 11 to 20
pf.services.times: every 15 minutes inside the restaurant's hours; same-day bookings until 1 hour before; up to 30 days ahead
pf.services.notBookings: delivery and takeout orders aren't bookings: not part of Rosie at launch
pf.services.nobodyHome: only for meal prep a chef leaves in the fridge; DONE with a photo

beforeTimes: party size (sets the table and whether a card is saved)
inside, patio or back room (patio times only in good weather)
for cooking away: the address, the guest count and the kitchen
afterTime: a high chair or a step-free way in
a cake to bring (the cake service)
securePageOnly: food allergies and diet needs: only on the secure page, with their own yes, shown only to the host and the kitchen for that booking
pf.questions.told: anyone ordering alcohol shows ID at the table (21 and over)
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult (18 or over) books for the party; a teen asks a parent; for an event at a venue, the person who rents it, or someone they authorize

words: a severe allergic reaction now: a swelling face or throat, trouble breathing
a fire, or a gas smell in the kitchen at a home event
pf.safety.what: the generic screen: call 911 now, no booking in that chat; Rosie gives no medical advice and names no medicine
pf.safety.goesOn: an allergy asked about for a future booking is not an emergency: it goes on the secure page, and booking continues

pf.first_steps.away: for events of 20 or more guests, a menu tasting at Lee's Bistro first, if the owner sets it; kitchen photos come with the quote
pf.first_steps.prep: the reminder says what's needed: arrive within the 15-minute grace time; for cooking at home, a clear counter, working oven and the guest count

pf.visit.checkIn: one check-in code per table, given at the host stand; the host texts it or types it on the Today page, or taps the name (marked done); away: the code from whoever is at the door
pf.visit.grace: 15 minutes after the time; then the host may give the table away and mark a no-show
pf.visit.atTheTable: the server checks the allergy note with the party before ordering, and checks ID for alcohol (21 and over), the restaurant's own steps
pf.visit.changes: a bigger party is seated only if a table fits; a cake service or anything extra is said before it's added
pf.visit.waitlist: a freed table is offered by text to one party at a time, 15 minutes to take it; walk-ins join the same list at the host stand
pf.visit.done: the check-in code (or the name tapped) proves the visit; away, DONE from the chef

pf.money.atTheRestaurant: nothing charged upfront; a card saved only for parties of 6 or more, if the owner wants it, only for a no-show or late-cancel fee the owner confirms; never a hold, deposit or the full price for a table
pf.money.fee: the owner's own fee, a set amount a person (the example's $20 a person); never more than the state's limit; no answer, no fee
pf.money.after: the bill is paid at the table, the restaurant's own way; Rosie texts no bill at the restaurant
pf.money.charges: any automatic gratuity or service charge (the example: 20% for 6 or more, all to the staff) is shown before the yes, in the confirmation and in the reminder
pf.money.tips: at the table, the restaurant's own way; on a bill Rosie texts for cooking away, a tip line if the owner turns it on
pf.money.away: the travel fee held, or a deposit once a quote is OK'd; the deposit cap from the state form
pf.money.tax: the restaurant's own; on a texted bill, the tax line the owner sets
pf.money.noSale: reservations are never sold or resold

pf.messages.neverInText: allergies, diet or health needs, gate or door codes
pf.messages.deleteAfter: an allergy note is shown only for that booking and deleted the morning after the visit; the booking keeps only 'note given, deleted on <date>'
pf.messages.minors: a teen's booking goes to a parent

pf.staff.byName: nobody is booked by name at the restaurant: the table is booked, and whoever runs the host stand checks the party in
pf.staff.roles: hosts (the host stand and the Today page), chefs (cooking away), bartenders (bar service)
pf.staff.licenses: a food handler card or an alcohol server permit for each person only where the state's rules require it
pf.staff.standIn: any host can run the host stand; a chef going away needs the caterer's skills set by the owner
pf.staff.oks: the owner (and the office manager, if set) OKs big parties, the back room and quotes over the limit

pf.rules.listing: where the state's rules require it, a signed listing agreement before any table is offered (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.fees: a no-show fee only with the customer's yes when booking, and only within the state's limits
pf.rules.alcohol: alcohol only to guests 21 or over with ID; bar service only under the liquor license
pf.rules.records: booking records 7 years; allergy notes deleted the morning after
pf.rules.showPermit: show a permit number where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.contracts: a written event agreement above the amount the state's rules set, for cooking away

pf.edges.partySize: the party grows or shrinks: re-seated if a table fits; dropping under 6 releases the saved card
pf.edges.lateParty: the table is held 15 minutes; a text saying they're late keeps it if a table is still free
pf.edges.runningBehind: the table before runs long: the host texts LATE, the party is told, and can change with no fee
pf.edges.noShow: marked by the host after the grace time; any fee only from a saved card, only once the owner confirms
pf.edges.weather: patio times close when the forecast is over the owner's limit; the party is offered inside or a new time
pf.edges.allergy: a severe allergy the kitchen can't serve safely: the party is told before the visit, and can cancel with no fee
pf.edges.walkIns: walk-ins join the walk-in list, apart from the booking waitlist; they pay at the table and carry no $2
pf.edges.waitlist: a full day: the party joins the waitlist; a freed table is offered to one party at a time, with 30 minutes to take it
pf.edges.sentNow: never: a table is booked ahead or walked in, and a chef shops and preps first, so nobody is on call
pf.edges.default: every other edge case is handled the generic way

notes:
Refit Oct 27 (REDESIGN 2 master): old words ops (74 in A) and ops on removed steps dropped; trade `more` lines kept (tables and rooms at sign-up; allergies only on the secure page; alcohol ID; the chef checks the allergy note); one words op on A4-62 (a restaurant's plug-in lists its tables); facts spaces, groups, tips; settings arrive A setstart, B window, cutoff A 24 hours before, B 2 days before; amounts per path with name (A fee $160 = $20 a person for 8); own record rows in A (pay.price / pay.left / pay.staff: free to book, the bill paid at the table); D66: no holds, the rest of a deposit on the saved card at the end or on the bill; rename pairs re-pointed to today's words.
Names: Sam Lee's main company is Lee Catering LLC (410 Main St; chefs cook and serve at a customer's home or event, with bar service as its second kind of work). His second company is Lee's Bistro LLC (36 Grove St), the restaurant. The master's shape is kept: flow A's story is at the second company (the restaurant), flow B's at the main one.
Staff: Devon and Mara are hosts at Lee's Bistro (the master's Riley and Avery); Nico and Lena are Lee Catering's chefs (Jordan and Casey). Nico also tends bar. Alex's home is 55 Cedar Ave.
Prices are the example's own, not a standard: set brunch $35 a person, kids brunch $15, cake service $20 a table, Chef's Table $140 a person, no-show fee $20 a person for 6 or more, a 20% tip for 6 or more; away: brunch at home for 4 $179, $89 travel fee, dinner party for 8 from photos $640, cooking class $150, dessert table $199.
Tables, not people, are booked at the restaurant: the master's space booking. Sign-up says the bistro books tables and lists them (S2-25, S2-26), and at A4-66 (what's booked) the restaurant takes 'A space or a table': A4-62 shows the open tables. Times show a table or an area (the long table, the patio), never a host. One check-in code covers the whole table, given at the host stand.
The plug-in's money for tables: the menu shows, nothing is charged upfront, a card is saved only for 6 or more (if the owner wants it, only for a fee the owner confirms), and the bill is paid at the table. So flow A turns off: photos and at-the-visit pricing, the hold, deposit and full-price branches, the rest due on a fixed day, the day-before hold, and the bill, saved-card and nothing-more branches after. No deposit on a starting price, so no visit+deposit path.
Flow A also turns off what never happens at a table: plans or insurance paying, a series of visits, video sessions, the first-step split (no first step for a table), class rosters, drop-offs, a bigger job, visits over several days, a child handed to an adult, results later, rented items, a crew one person short, a host's set date, something required missing, and a storage fee for something left behind.
A host out, a host's day off or last day: the master's 'no person booked' branches (A7-60, S11-88, S11-91, D37). Sam names who covers, and no booking moves. The 'booked by name' branches are off in flow A; flow B (chefs) keeps them and turns the 'not by name' ones off.
The automatic tip for 6 or more is named before the yes, in the confirmation and the reminder (master rule S13-17, plus a gap).
Allergies are a sensitive answer under the master's rule S13-05: asked only on the secure page with their own yes, shown only to the host and kitchen (or the chef), checked at the table, and deleted the morning after (plug-in pf.messages, plus a more line on S13-05).
Alcohol: anyone ordering it shows ID to the server, 21 and over: the restaurant's own check, not a Rosie step. Bar service away needs the liquor license and a bartender's own permit where the state's rules require it.
Waitlist: the master's (A4-15 'Joins the waitlist', A4-60, A4-61): a freed table goes by text to one party at a time, 30 minutes each. Walk-ins wait for a table that fits (A3-32's 'A table or space that fits', A3-34), pay at the table and carry no $2.
Delivery and takeout aren't bookings: the AI is told so, and nothing is booked.
Owner's OK: parties up to 10 book at once; the back room (11 to 20) asks Sam first. The main story (8) books at once.
Flow B maps the home-repair what-ifs to cooking: a landlord's OK becomes a venue's OK, a landlord paying becomes a company paying, a part becomes a special order, a hazard is a frayed oven cord, damage is a chipped platter, the rented fan becomes rented chafing dishes, the faucet left at the shop becomes a cake stand.
Flow B turns off quotes at the visit (cooking is priced before), plan or insurance paying, a part going to the shop, and a report ready later. The full price stays on for Lee Catering (a ticketed cooking class can be prepaid) but isn't one of the profession's paths.
Flow B keeps the master's 2-hour arrival windows; the dinner party's 8-10am window covers shopping and prep.
Warranties: a meal carries none. The master's warranty claim becomes a make-good (a free dessert or a free return visit), always Sam's call.
Large rename lists carry whole master sentences (sentence pairs first, then words), so the overlay keeps few ops while both flows read as restaurant and catering work.
Neither company takes jobs sent now: S2-30 takes 'No: never sent now' (S2-31), and flow B takes 'Never sent now' at B4-81 (B4-82 shows the soonest times), B7-55 and B8-58, with the sent-now branches off (B4-16, B6-03).
Flow B also turns off the outside check partway (B8-65) and the permit inspection after the visit; a landlord's top amount becomes the company's, and the storage fee follows the cake stand.
Plug-in splits (master v1.2, D24): each company needs its permit and pays the $2 (S1-60, S1-62, S1-63, S1-65, S11-92, S11-94); each person has a permit where the state's rules require one (S2-28); no classes on a timetable (S2-32); no children's ban (A4-70); no damage hold when booked (A5-24, B5-26); a table is held 15 minutes when the party runs late (A7-70); nothing is left at a restaurant (A8-53); a meal is rated (A10-34). Flow A: no first step or form (A4-43). Flow B: a tasting first for events of 20 or more (B4-38 'Yes'), arrival windows (B4-83), the venue or company matters (B4-78), and a chef booked by name, or a date that can't move, or a crew (B7-56).
Whole what-ifs that never happen at a table stay off at their branch (a crew one short, a host's set date, too few booked to run, a form not done); their plug-in splits go with them.
Final pass (FIX-pilot-final): Pat OKs only Lee Catering prices over $500 (S1-47). Plug-in splits decided: B4-83 keeps only arrival windows (a seat and 'No person named' off), B8-67 an adult must be there; splitsKept (every branch, service by service): S1-29 (a listing agreement only where the state's rules require it), S2-25 (the bistro books tables, Lee Catering books chefs), B4-57 (an event agreement over the amount), B8-69 and B8-70 (meal prep with nobody home; a dinner party needs someone home), B8-71 (rented tables delivered and set up, or no delivery). B9-27's 'Not today' and 'OK some lines' are off: catering is never priced at the door.
Review (Oct 22, evening): A10-01 sends no text on the nothing-saved path (the restaurant's variant had lost the master's 'sends nothing'); S1-30 names the listing agreement, not a health privacy agreement; A7-02's 'A plan charge is due' is off and Owen's standing table is paid at the table; leftover barber and plumbing words cleared (perms, a patch test for hair dye, a barber's chair, camera inspections, a rating plate, a yard drain 'clearing', a new water heater, a lead-safe notice, rentals in Morgan's plan, 'Lee Catering'' without its s); the cooking class plan reads monthly throughout; the first step in flow B is a menu tasting, not an estimate visit.
Touch-up 2 (Oct 23): Ben's no-show (S11-23 to S11-28) follows the card rule. On the card path it's his Fri table for 6, so a card was saved, and the fee is $20 a person for 6: $120 (asked, charged, reminded). On the nothing-taken path it's a table for 4: no card, so no fee. The fee-free what-if (S11-35) names no party size, since it shows on both paths. His Sat 10:00am table for 4 on the day list (A8-01) is a different booking and saves no card.
Touch-up 2, part 2 (Oct 23): Dee's same-day patio lunch (S11-03, S11-04) is a party of 6, so her saved card follows the rule: only for the $20-a-person fee, said in her confirmation. Her later 'card was only saved' lines (S11-06, S11-84, S11-86) and the long-table offer (S11-80) stay right. The AI preview (S11-57) says tables for 1 to 5 take nothing, and 6 or more save a card only for the $20-a-person fee.
